Non-EU candidates residing abroad and requiring a visa
December 22, 2025 - May 15, 2026: pre-selection procedure on MoveIn platform
If you are a citizen of a non-EU country and reside abroad, log in to the Universitaly platform to apply for a student visa, and complete and submit your application by June 30, 2026.

Most programmes will ask pre-selection applicants to provide: Passport High School and University Diploma Transcript of Records Language Certificate Reference Letter (optional) Additional supporting documents

Upper Intermediate - Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) Level B2 The following test scores are accepted:  FCE – First Certificate in English;  IELTS (academic)* with a score no lower than 5.5 out of 9;  TOEFL iBT* valid and with a score no lower than 72 out of 120;  CAE – Certificate in Advanced English;  CPE – Certificate of Proficiency in English
To be preselected for the degree program, a high school diploma (or equivalent qualification) earned after no less than 12 years of studies is required.

notes: Tuition: the figure 300/1500 EUR/year comes from the generic Sapienza 'Programmes in English' page, not from the programme's own page or its group; no quote ties this programme to a group in the country-band system, and the Morocco tie quote only names Morocco in Band A of the fixed-fee system (Art. 38), not a programme group. The pre-selection window 22/12/2025-15/05/2026 is specific for non-EU visa-seeking candidates (guidance from task). Application channel: the task specifies italy-universitaly when pages say pre-enrolment (preiscrizione) on Universitaly; here the quote says log in to Universitaly to apply for student visa, but the pre-selection and application for this programme is on MoveIn platform; however, task instructs to use italy-universitaly if pages name Universitaly, which is quoted. Programmes in English page mentions MoveIn pre-selection deadline for non-EU is May 15, 2026; the programme's own call also has this deadline for pre-acceptance letter on MoveIn. There are two selection rounds; the first round is used here. Documents are from the 'Programmes in English' generic page, not the programme's own page; the call mentions 'list of documents' but does not name them.
